subject.title: Add Tailscale Serve support for WSL gateways

question: Should generated WSL gateways support optional `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true`, making verified Tailscale identity and tailnet ACLs a maintained gateway authorization path?
rationale: The code separates transport from identity trust and has strong proof, but deciding whether tailnet identity is a supported core authorization contract is a lasting product and security policy choice that implementation review cannot make alone.

options.title: Approve opt-in identity trust
options.body: Accept the documented opt-in authorization model, retain root-owned Tailscale lifecycle control, and require the refreshed rebased validation before merge.

options.title: Support private transport only
options.body: Keep Tailscale Serve for private WSS connectivity but remove the identity-trust option and continue requiring OpenClaw token or paired-device authentication.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers want to own the Tailscale authorization and lifecycle contract in core.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in identity trust
recommendation.body: Accept the documented opt-in authorization model, retain root-owned Tailscale lifecycle control, and require the refreshed rebased validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history is the clearest ownership signal for generated-gateway onboarding and the supported authentication model this PR would extend.
